Date: 2028-07-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Compute hedge & SLA gap mapping — Helios AI Dedicated commit

Sara — following up from our call this morning. Thanks for the walkthrough of Helios's production traffic profile. Per our discussion I attached an initial sizing model (commit_sizing_model_v3.xlsx) and a CSV with the ingest/session mix we used (helios_ingest_profile.csv). Highlights from our side: 

- Baseline model: redwood-ql-13b-4bit (quantized). We assume token generation efficiency ~600 tokens/sec per GPU slab under the observed prompt length distribution (median request ~260 tokens, but 95th ~1,200 tokens).
- SLO target: p95 response latency <= 250ms for interactive routes (inference-only, no heavy tool calls).
- Expected committed steady-state token rate after launch: 45M tokens/day (~520 tokens/sec average sustained across daily active window). Peak bursts: short spikes up to ~1500 concurrent concurrent-user flows for ~5-12 minute windows, translating to transient token/sec of ~18k–22k.
- Recommendation (initial): Dedicated commit of 9 slabs (each slab = 4x A100-equivalent inference partitions in our model), which maps to ~5.4M token/sec capacity headroom under our batching assumptions and KV-cache warm paths. That gives ~30% operational headroom vs expected peaks and leaves room for autoscale/burst pool of 2 slabs for unexpected surges.

Asks: can you confirm the expected percent of long-form generations (requests >800 tokens) vs short replies? The % matters for tail latency and batch efficiency. Also, please confirm whether Helios plans to route all traffic through a single region (us-west) or multi-region with fallbacks — that changes cold-cache behavior and reserve sizing.

Next steps we propose: Priyom will share the per-slab p95/p99 latency curves for redwood-ql variants and a simple Monte Carlo run that simulates 24-hr burst behavior using your ingest CSV. If that looks good, we'll update the MAP and surface commit tiers + pricing.

Thanks,
Avery

Thanks Avery — quick answers inline: 

1) Long-form %: roughly 12–15% of requests generate >800 tokens. Most of those are batched analytical requests between 02:00–05:00 UTC and are latency-tolerant. The interactive product front-end (our primary SLA route) is ~75% of volume and averages 200–350 tokens.

2) Regions: initial launch will be single-region (us-west) for compliance reasons, with a DR region (us-east) for failover. We expect 97% of traffic in us-west initially.

3) Bursts: spikes typically align with market open/close events (15–20 minutes), and one-off product campaigns can create sustained +48 hour elevated load.

Attached is a sample 24-hour telemetry dump from last month's beta (helios_telemetry_sample.csv). Let us know if you need additional cadence breakdowns.

—Sara

Sara / Avery — I ran the Monte Carlo with the telemetry sample + the ingest profile. Quick technical summary and explicit numbers so leadership can see the tradeoffs: 

Model & perf assumptions (conservative):
- redwood-ql-13b-4bit: 600 tokens/sec per slab sustained average; 450 tokens/sec per slab under 95th-percentile prompt mix (longer tails reduce batching efficiency).
- p95 latency with KV warm cache and continuous batching: ~220ms at 450 tokens/sec per slab. p99 ~420ms for the same operating point.

Sizing outputs (24-hr sim, 10k runs):
- Commit of 7 slabs -> median unmet peak events per day: 6; p95 latency breaches on interactive route: 14% of peak windows.
- Commit of 9 slabs -> median unmet peak events per day: 1; p95 latency breaches on interactive route: 2.4%.
- Commit of 11 slabs -> effectively zero unmet peak events; average utilization ~68% with 40% headroom for sustained campaigns.

Recommended configuration: 
- Commit 9 slabs (primary) + 2-slab dedicated burst pool that can be claimed during campaign windows (policy-controlled, billed usage beyond commit). That balances monthly cost vs frequency of bursts you described.
- Maintain a cold-cache mitigation plan by pre-warming KV for top-1000 prefixes before anticipated campaign start times (we can automate via Redwood Console runbook hooks).
- Latency SLO controls: enable per-route batching cap at 250ms and aggressive prefix caching on interactive routes.

Notes on alternatives: if Helios is willing to accept a slightly higher p95 (~300ms) in exchange for fewer committed slabs, we can reduce commit to 7 slabs and rely on an expanded burst pool (4 slabs) + 1.5x autoscale throttle during campaign windows. That leans more on ops rather than commit.

I've attached the sim outputs and a summarized table in commit_sizing_model_v3.xlsx (sheet: MC_summary). Monica — please add an ops note about pre-warm automation and RBAC needs.

—Priyom
